query: What travel policy risks appear in expense descriptions?

per_column.name: expense_type_label
per_column.rationale: Categorises each expense from the short_description into meaningful types (travel vs asset vs service). This gives a genuine grouping axis to isolate travel expenses, which is the entry point for the travel-policy-risk query. Sample values are sound readings of the descriptions.

per_column.name: travel_item_hardware_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Directly targets a travel policy risk: travel-labelled expenses that reference hardware/asset items. Highly relevant to the query. Derivable by comparing short_description and ci fields. Samples are all False and consistent with non-travel rows, though the inference logic is only partially verifiable from provided samples.

per_column.name: personal_vs_business_ambiguity
per_column.rationale: Flags a classic travel policy risk (personal vs business expense ambiguity), squarely on-query. Warranted as an inference from description text. Samples are False and consistent, but the True cases are not shown, so groundedness is moderate.

per_column.name: ci_name_anomaly
per_column.rationale: Flags anomalies in the ci field. Only loosely tied to travel policy risk; more of a data-quality signal. Derivable from the ci column, samples plausibly False for standard hardware names, but analytical leverage for THIS query is limited.

per_column.name: source_id_present
per_column.rationale: A trivial presence flag on an existing column; near-mechanical and only weakly connected to travel policy risk. Fully grounded (directly checks whether source_id exists), but adds little analytical leverage for the query.

per_column.name: processing_lag_risk
per_column.rationale: Bucketises the gap around processed_date. Well grounded from date fields, but processing lag is an operational/timeliness signal, not a travel-policy-in-descriptions risk. Marginal relevance to the specific query.

per_column.name: entry_method
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes manual vs auto-generated vs self-input, readable from description wording ('Automated'/'Automatically' => auto). Grounded and a real axis, but only indirectly related to travel policy risk in descriptions.

per_column.name: department_travel_alignment
per_column.rationale: Compares whether a travel expense aligns with the department that would be expected to travel ('travel_unexpected' is a real policy red flag). On-query and provides a cross-column grouping axis. Derivable from department + expense type, though the expected/unexpected inference is only partly verifiable from samples.

judge.rationale: Several columns (travel_item_hardware_mismatch, personal_vs_business_ambiguity, department_travel_alignment, expense_type_label) directly serve the travel-policy-risk query and provide genuine grouping/flagging axes. Others (source_id_present, processing_lag_risk, ci_name_anomaly, entry_method) are grounded and mechanically sound but only tangentially tied to this specific query, dragging usefulness to moderate. Groundedness is generally strong: the shown values are sound readings of description/date/ci fields with no observed hallucinations, though the True-flag logic for the risk columns is not fully demonstrated in the samples.
